correctness.rationale: For each \(t\), \(P^*\delta_t\) is a probability measure and decomposes as \(d(t)\delta_t\) plus a positive measure singular to \(\delta_t\). Thus \(\|(P-M_f)^*\delta_t\|=1-d(t)+|d(t)-f(t)|\). Taking the supremum over point evaluations gives the operator norm. The focal proof gives \(d(t)\ge\alpha\) for all \(t\) and an attained value \(d(t_0)=\alpha\), which yields the exact distance, the if-and-only-if best-approximant interval, and the scalar profile. All quantifiers and the \(\alpha=1\) boundary are covered; no finite computation substitutes for proof.

value.rationale: The result identifies the order-theoretic Wickstead parameter as an exact metric invariant: \(1-\alpha\) is the distance of \(P\) to the entire multiplication-operator subspace. It also characterizes every best multiplication approximant pointwise and gives the full scalar-axis norm profile, so it is stronger and structurally more informative than a single complementary-projection norm calculation. The statement is natural for a theorem whose central diagonal is defined through multiplication operators.
